Research question: "What analyses or measurements would best test whether AP-1 acts as a cellular memory mechanism?"

Propose 5 distinct, concrete ideas (analyses, measurements, or experiments) that a research lab could pursue to address this question. For each idea give a short title and a description of one or two sentences.

ideas.title: Transient-pulse persistence assay ("nothing gold can stay" decay kinetics)
ideas.description: Give cells a brief, defined stimulus (e.g., EGF/TPA/anisomycin pulse) and track AP-1 (FOS/JUN) protein, chromatin occupancy, and target gene expression by live reporters and time-course CUT&RUN well after the stimulus ends. Fit decay curves to distinguish a fleeting early peak (like the first gold leaf fading) from a self-sustaining state that persists for many cell divisions, and test whether persistence outlasts the half-lives of AP-1 proteins and mRNAs.

ideas.title: Chromatin accessibility memory with AP-1 degron/acute depletion
ideas.description: After a priming stimulus, use ATAC-seq and CUT&Tag for H3K27ac/H3K4me1 to identify loci that stay open once the stimulus is gone. Then acutely degrade FOS/JUN (dTAG/AID) either during priming only or after priming only, to test whether AP-1 is needed to establish versus maintain the accessible state, a distinction that separates a memory mechanism from a transient trigger.

ideas.title: Re-stimulation (primed vs naive) response test
ideas.description: Compare transcriptional response magnitude and speed to a second stimulus in primed versus naive cells at varying rest intervals, using RNA-seq and single-cell readouts. Plot the memory decay vs. rest time and ask whether AP-1 motif-containing enhancers show faster/stronger induction, and whether AP-1 dominant-negative (e.g., A-FOS) expressed only during priming abolishes the enhanced second response.

ideas.title: Single-cell lineage tracing of AP-1 states across divisions
ideas.description: Use live-cell AP-1 activity reporters (e.g., endogenously tagged FOS/JUN or a TRE-driven fluorescent reporter) with time-lapse imaging of mother-daughter pairs to measure whether AP-1 activity state is inherited and correlated between sister cells beyond what shared stimulus explains. Quantify autocorrelation across generations to distinguish heritable bistable states from re-induced noise.

ideas.title: Synthetic AP-1 pioneer-site perturbation and mitotic bookmarking
ideas.description: Use CRISPR to mutate or dCas9-block specific AP-1 motifs at candidate memory enhancers, and perform mitotic-arrest CUT&RUN/imaging to test whether AP-1 stays on mitotic chromosomes as a bookmark. Test necessity and sufficiency by seeing whether motif loss erases the retained accessibility and primed response, and whether tethering JUN/FOS to a naive locus can create a durable open state after release.
